question: All roses are flowers. All flowers need sunlight. Which conclusion must be true?

options.C: Some flowers do not need sunlight

explanation: Transitive syllogism: roses→flowers→need sunlight, so all roses need sunlight.

question:
Some chairs are tables. All tables are furniture. No furniture is a toy. Which conclusion definitely follows?
I. Some chairs are not toys.
II. All furniture is a chair.
explanation: Some chairs are tables→furniture→not toys, so some chairs are not toys (I). II fails because only 'some' chairs are tables, not all furniture is a chair.

question: All successful companies invest in R&D. Company Z does not invest in R&D. What follows?

options.C: Company Z may still be successful
options.D: Some successful companies don't invest in R&D

explanation: Contrapositive: if a company does not invest in R&D, it is not successful.

question:
Statements: (1) All poets are artists. (2) Some artists are scientists. (3) All scientists are logical. (4) No logical person is irrational.
Conclusions: I. Some poets are scientists. II. Some artists are not irrational.
explanation: I cannot be concluded: all poets are artists but not all artists are scientists. II follows: some artists are scientists→logical→not irrational.

question: If Ahmed is tired, he takes a nap. Ahmed did NOT take a nap. What can we conclude?

options.C: Ahmed was tired but chose not to sleep

explanation: Contrapositive of 'tired→nap' is 'no nap→not tired'.

question: A smartphone has 5G only if it has a Snapdragon or Exynos chip. Phone X has 5G but does NOT have an Exynos chip. What follows?

options.B: Phone X has a Snapdragon chip

explanation: 5G→(Snapdragon OR Exynos). X has 5G and not Exynos, so X must have Snapdragon.

question: Rules: (1) Pass exam→eligible for scholarship. (2) Eligible AND good attendance→receives scholarship. (3) Zara received scholarship. What can be concluded?

options.B: Zara passed the exam and maintained good attendance

explanation: Scholarship requires both eligibility (from passing) and good attendance. Since she received it, both conditions must hold.

question: Given: (1) If P then Q. (2) If Q then R. (3) If R then S. (4) If T then not-S. (5) T is true. What can be deduced about P?

options.C: P may be true or false

explanation: T→not-S (4,5). Contra of (3): not-S→not-R. Contra of (2): not-R→not-Q. Contra of (1): not-Q→not-P.

question: Argument: 'Literacy rates rose and unemployment fell simultaneously. Literacy causes lower unemployment.' Which STRENGTHENS this?

options.A: Both changes happened in the same city
options.B: Literacy improvements preceded the unemployment drop by 2 years
options.C: Other countries also have low unemployment

explanation: Temporal precedence (literacy improved before unemployment fell) supports the causal direction, ruling out reverse causation.

question: Argument: 'Mobile phone use among teens increased, and teen anxiety increased. Phone use causes anxiety.' Which WEAKENS this most?

options.A: Adults with phones also report some anxiety
options.B: Anxious teens tend to use phones more as an escape
options.D: Social media is a smartphone feature

explanation: Reverse causation — anxiety may cause phone use, not vice versa. This undermines the causal claim.

question: Argument: 'City M installed speed cameras; traffic fatalities fell 20%. Speed cameras save lives.' What MOST weakens this?

options.B: A major new trauma hospital opened in City M during the same period
options.C: Other cities also use speed cameras

explanation: An alternative explanation (better hospital care) could fully account for the drop in fatalities, undermining the causal claim.

question: Argument: 'Students sleeping ≥8 hours score 15% higher on tests. We should mandate 8-hour sleep before exams.' What MOST undermines the policy?

options.B: Disciplined students naturally sleep more AND score higher; mandating sleep won't change discipline
options.C: Sleeping more than 10 hours is counterproductive

explanation: A third variable (discipline) causes both good sleep and high scores. Mandating sleep won't instil discipline, so scores won't improve.

question: Argument: 'We should hire Salman because he has 5 years of relevant experience.' Underlying assumption:

options.A: Salman is cheaper than other candidates
options.B: Experience is a reliable predictor of success in this role
options.C: 5 years is the maximum experience among applicants

explanation: The argument only holds if experience in this context predicts job performance.

question: Argument: 'This drug reduced cholesterol in rats; it will therefore be effective for humans.' Key assumption:

options.A: Rats and humans share identical diets
options.B: Cholesterol regulation mechanisms are sufficiently similar in rats and humans
options.C: The drug has no side effects in rats
options.D: Humans need lower cholesterol than rats

explanation: The argument assumes the rat model is applicable to humans — i.e., similar biological mechanisms exist.

question: Argument: 'Library membership fell; people are reading less, so we should cut library funding.' Key assumption:

options.A: Libraries serve no purpose other than book lending
options.B: Falling membership reflects reduced reading, not a shift to e-books or other formats
options.C: Digital books cost more than physical ones
options.D: Library funding comes from membership fees

explanation: The argument assumes membership equals reading. If people shifted to e-books, membership could fall without reduced reading.

question: Argument: 'Country A spends 8% of GDP on education — double Country B — yet Country B produces more Nobel laureates per capita. Therefore, spending is not the key driver of academic excellence.' The argument's key assumption is:

options.A: Nobel laureates are a valid measure of academic excellence
options.B: Country A has a larger population
options.C: Both countries have spent at these levels for decades

explanation: The argument implicitly equates Nobel laureates per capita with academic excellence. If this metric is flawed, the conclusion collapses.

question: Paradox: A farmer used more fertiliser this season yet harvested less crop. What best explains this?

options.B: Excess fertiliser became toxic to the crops, damaging root systems
options.C: Other farmers also increased fertiliser use
options.D: Weather conditions were identical to last year

explanation: Over-fertilisation can chemically burn or poison plants, reducing yield despite greater input.

question: Paradox: A company increased customer-service staff by 50%, yet average complaint-resolution time increased. What best explains this?

options.B: New staff were poorly trained and escalated issues instead of resolving them
options.C: The company expanded its product line

explanation: Untrained staff generate longer escalation chains rather than resolving issues directly, increasing average resolution time.

question: Paradox: A country achieved record food production yet its hunger index worsened. What best explains this?

options.A: The country exported the majority of its food surplus
options.B: The population declined during the year

explanation: Exporting the surplus leaves domestic supply unchanged or reduced; high production can coexist with domestic hunger.

question: Paradox: A tech firm introduced a 4-day work week. Individual productivity rose 20%, but total project completion rates fell 10%. What best explains this?

options.A: Employees worked harder during their 4 days
options.B: Individual output improved but increased hand-off complexity created bottlenecks in collaborative workflows

explanation: Individual gains can mask systemic coordination costs — more handoffs per time unit create delays that reduce overall project throughput.

question: A student scores: Physics=70, Chemistry=85, Biology=60, Maths=90, English=75. What is the average score?
A shop sold 200 items in January. Sales rose 15% in February. How many items were sold in February?
Quarterly revenue (PKR lakhs): Q1=120, Q2=144, Q3=172.8. Revenue grows at the same % each quarter. What is Q4 revenue?
Departmental expenses: HR=20%, Operations=35%, Marketing=25%, IT=15%, Admin=5%. Total budget = PKR 80 lakhs. How much more does Operations spend than IT?
explanation: Operations: 0.35×80=28 lakhs. IT: 0.15×80=12 lakhs. Difference: 28−12=16 lakhs.

question: Product X sells at PKR 500 with a 40% profit margin (on selling price). Product Y sells at PKR 800 with a 25% profit margin. If 300 units of X and 200 units of Y are sold, what is the total profit?
Four people W, X, Y, Z sit in a row. Y is leftmost. X is immediately right of Y. Z is rightmost. What is W's position from the left?
explanation: Y=1, X=2, Z=4 (rightmost), so W=3 (3rd from left).

question: Five people A–E sit in a row. D is 3rd (middle). A is immediately right of D. E is immediately left of D. B is leftmost. Where is C?
explanation: B=1, E=2, D=3, A=4, C=5. C is at the right end.

question: Six friends M–R sit in a row. R=position 6. Q is immediately left of R. M=position 1. N is immediately right of M. P is between N and Q (strictly between). O is not adjacent to Q. What is O's position?
explanation: M=1,N=2,Q=5,R=6. P between N(2) and Q(5): P=3 or 4. O not adjacent to Q(5)→O≠4,6. Remaining positions 3,4 for P,O; O≠4→O=3, P=4.

question: Five students A–E in a row. Clues: A=position 1. B=position 4. E=position 2. C is strictly between A and B (not at ends). D is not at position 2. What is D's position?
explanation: A=1,E=2,B=4. C between A(1) and B(4) but E=2, so C=3. D=5 (only remaining, and D≠2 is satisfied).

question: Six people sit in a row. F=1, E=6. A is not at either end and not adjacent to F. B is at an even position and adjacent to C. C is immediately left of D. What is A's position?
explanation: F=1,E=6. A not at end→A∈{2,3,4,5}; A not adjacent to F(1)→A≠2. C immediately left of D; B adjacent to C and at even position. Testing (C=3,D=4): B=2(even, adjacent to C=3)✓. Remaining A,E=6 for pos 5. A=5 ✓.

question: Four people A–D sit in a circle facing the center. A is directly opposite B. C is immediately clockwise from A. What is D's position relative to C?
explanation: A=1,B=3 (opposite). C=2 (immediately CW from A). D=4. C(2) and D(4) are directly opposite each other.

question: Six people P–U sit in a circle. P is directly opposite Q (positions 1 & 4). R is immediately clockwise from P (pos 2). S is directly opposite R (pos 5). U=pos 3, T=pos 6. Who is directly opposite U?
explanation: U=position 3; in a 6-person circle, the seat directly opposite pos 3 is pos 6 = T.

question: Eight people A–H sit in a circle (facing center). A=1, E=5 (opposite). B=3 (2 seats CW from A). C=7 (opposite B). D=6 (immediately CW from E). H=2 (opposite D). G=8 (immediately CCW from A). Who is immediately clockwise from G (pos 8)?
explanation: G is at position 8; the next seat clockwise is position 1 = A.

question: Six people sit in a circle (facing center): A=1, C=4 (opposite A). B is not adjacent to A. D is immediately clockwise from B. E and F are adjacent. F is between D and C going clockwise from D. E is not adjacent to C. What is D's position?
explanation: B∉{2,6} (not adjacent to A=1)→B∈{3,5}. If B=5: D=6. F between D(6) and C(4) CW: 6→1→2→3→4; F=2 or 3. E adjacent to F; E not adjacent to C(4)→E≠3,5. If F=3,E=2 or F=2,E=3(excluded). So F=3,E=2. D=6 ✓.

question: Rania says, 'Tariq's father is my grandfather's only son.' What is Tariq's relation to Rania?
explanation: Grandfather's only son = Rania's father. Tariq's father = Rania's father → Tariq is Rania's brother.

question: Looking at a portrait, Hamid says, 'She is the daughter of my father's only son.' Who is the person in the portrait to Hamid?
explanation: Father's only son = Hamid himself. Daughter of Hamid = Hamid's daughter.

question: A is B's mother. C is A's husband. D is C's father. E is D's wife. F is B's sister. How is E related to F?
explanation: C=B's father. D=C's father=B's paternal grandfather. E=D's wife=B's paternal grandmother. F is B's sister → E is also F's paternal grandmother.

question: X is Y's brother. Y is Z's daughter. Z is W's wife. W is V's son. U is V's wife. How is X related to U?
explanation: Y's mother=Z; Z's husband=W=X's father. W's father=V; V's wife=U. So U is X's paternal grandmother → X is U's grandson.

question: P is Q's father. R is P's mother. S is R's husband. T is Q's sister. U is T's mother. How is S related to U?
explanation: T's mother=U=P's wife (since T and Q are P's children). S=R's husband=P's father. U is P's wife → S is U's father-in-law.

question: Sadia starts facing East. She turns 90° clockwise, then 180° counterclockwise. What direction is she now facing?
explanation: East +90°CW = South. South +180°CCW = North.

question: Imran walks 8 km North, then 6 km East, then 8 km South. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
explanation: North 8 and South 8 cancel out. Net displacement = 6 km East.

question: Farah walks 12 km East, then 9 km South, then 12 km West. How far is she from her starting point?
explanation: East 12 and West 12 cancel. Net displacement = 9 km South.

question: A man walks: 10 km North, 8 km East, 4 km South, 3 km West, 6 km South. What is his straight-line displacement from the start?
explanation: N: 10−4−6=0. E: 8−3=5. Net displacement = 5 km East.

question: If MANGO is coded by shifting each letter +1 (A→B, B→C … Z→A), how is APPLE coded?
explanation: A→B, P→Q, P→Q, L→M, E→F = BQQMF.

question: In a code language: 'red sky high' = 'X Y Z'; 'high moon rise' = 'Z P Q'; 'red moon fall' = 'X P R'. What is the code for 'sky'?
explanation: 'red'=X (sentences 1,3). 'high'=Z (sentences 1,2). 'moon'=P (sentences 2,3). 'sky' is the remaining word in sentence 1 → Y.

question: In a code each letter is shifted 2 places backward (A→Y, B→Z, C→A, D→B …). How is WINDOW coded?
explanation: W→U, I→G, N→L, D→B, O→M, W→U = UGLBMU.

question: In a code each letter is shifted forward by its position in the word (1st letter +1, 2nd +2, 3rd +3, 4th +4). How is BEST coded?
In a class of 40 students, Umar ranks 12th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
explanation: Rank from bottom = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29.

question: Six athletes finish a race. P finishes before Q. Q before T. R finishes between P and Q (strictly). S finishes after T. U finishes after S. What is T's finishing position?
explanation: Order: P → R → Q → T → S → U. T finishes 4th.

question: Seven employees ranked 1–7 (1=best). Ali ranks better than Bilal. Bilal ranks better than Chaudhry. Faisal ranks better than Bilal. Daniyal ranks worse than Faisal but better than Ghazala. Ehsan is exactly 4th. What is Bilal's rank?
explanation: Both Ali and Faisal rank above Bilal (occupying positions 1 and 2). Ehsan=4. Therefore Bilal must be 3rd.
